thread.previously: A high-speed train and a regional train collided near Toledo on 27 Oct 2026. The toll rose over four days as rescuers reached the rear carriages.
thread.changed: Investigators now say the signal that should have stopped the regional train was showing green, which points at the control system rather than the driver.

stories.headline: Spain's train crash: a green light that should have been red
stories.question: How can a modern rail network let two trains onto the same track?
stories.dek: Investigators say a signal showed green when it should have shown red. That turns a tragedy into a question about the software every European railway is installing.

so_far.text: On 27 October a high-speed train hit a regional train near Toledo, killing 68 people, Spain's deadliest rail accident in more than a decade. Rescue took four days. The government ordered an inquiry and suspended services on the line while the wreckage was cleared.

what_happened.text: On 2 November the rail accident investigation board published its first findings. The signal protecting the junction showed green to the regional train even though the high-speed train already had the route. Data recorders show both drivers were within the speed limit. The board said the fault lay in how the signalling system's two computers disagreed about which train owned the track, and that the backup check did not catch it.

lesson.concept: How railway signals keep two trains apart
lesson.big_idea: Track is split into blocks, and a computer lets only one train into each block at a time by turning its signal green.

steps.title: Track is split into blocks
steps.text: Each stretch of line is a block. Sensors tell the control computer whether a train is inside it.

steps.title: One train per block
steps.text: The computer turns a block's entrance signal green only when the block is empty, and red otherwise.

steps.title: Junctions need agreement
steps.text: Where two lines meet, both control computers must agree who owns the junction before either signal clears.

steps.title: A mismatch must stop everything
steps.text: If the two pictures differ, a safety check should turn every signal red until people sort it out.

example.setup: Say two trains, A and B, both want a junction block, and train A asked first.
example.result: The system is only as safe as the check that catches two computers disagreeing.

apply.text: Investigators say the check meant to catch the mismatch failed silently, so the regional train saw green on a junction the high-speed train already held.

practice.q: If three trains wait for one junction block, how many can have a green signal at once?
practice.answer: Only one. The block allows one train; the other two see red until it leaves.

steps.text: Modern lines divide track into blocks, and only one train may hold a block at a time.
Computers grant blocks and turn the signal at each block's entrance red or green.
At Toledo two control computers held different pictures of who owned the junction.
The check meant to catch that mismatch failed silently, so the wrong train saw green.

items.name: Óscar Puente

items.meaning: more than double Spain's last major crash, Angrois in 2013 (80 dead) excepted
the system runs two in parallel so one can catch the other's mistakes

analogy.text: Think of two air-traffic controllers sharing one runway, each with their own screen. The rule is that both must agree before a plane lands. At Toledo the screens disagreed, and the rule that should have frozen everything didn't fire.
analogy.breaks: Unlike air traffic, a train can't swerve: once a signal clears, the driver has no way to see the other train in time.

items.view: Says the fault was a rare software condition and that a patch is already on every similar junction.
Says drivers warned of 'phantom greens' on this line in 2025 and were ignored.

for_you.text: Indian Railways is rolling out Kavach, its own automatic train protection system, on 1,500 km of track a year. Toledo shows why the hard part is not the hardware but making sure two systems never disagree in silence.

misconception.myth: Automatic signalling removes human error, so crashes like this can't happen any more.
misconception.fact: It moves the risk into software: the system can still be wrong, and when it is, drivers trust it.

next.text: The full report is due within a year. Parliament questions the minister on 5 November, and Adif must show regulators its fix within 30 days.
unknowns: Whether the same fault exists on other lines

check.why: Both drivers were within the limit; the signalling system's two computers held different pictures of the track.

The death toll reached 68 on Friday after rescuers recovered the last bodies from the rear carriages.
Investigators said the signal showed a proceed aspect to the regional train.

Kavach has been commissioned on a further 1,465 route km this year.

scenes.say: How can a modern railway let two trains onto the same track? In Spain last week, that is exactly what happened.
Near Toledo, south of Madrid, a high-speed train hit a regional train. Sixty-eight people died.
Investigators now say the regional train saw a green signal. It should have been red.
The system uses two computers that must agree on which train owns each piece of track. At Toledo they disagreed, and the backup check failed silently.
India is installing its own system, called Kavach, on fifteen hundred kilometres of track a year.
The lesson: automation moves the risk into software. The minister faces parliament on Thursday.

takeaways: Spain's train crash: a green light that should have been red.

thread.previously: Delhi's air quality has been 'very poor' since late October, as farm fires and still winter air trap pollution over the city.
thread.changed: The air quality panel moved Delhi to Stage III of its emergency plan, banning older diesel trucks and pausing construction.

stories.headline: Delhi bans old trucks as smog thickens
stories.question: Will banning old diesel trucks actually clear Delhi's air?
stories.dek: Delhi has moved to stage III of its pollution emergency plan. The rules bite hardest on trucks and building sites, but most of the smog comes from elsewhere.

so_far.text: Every winter Delhi's air turns toxic. Cooler, still air traps smoke from crop burning in Punjab and Haryana, plus traffic, dust and industry. In 2025 the city recorded 24 'severe' days. This season's AQI crossed 300 on 25 October.

what_happened.text: On 1 November the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) invoked Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) across Delhi-NCR after the average AQI rose past 350. Stage III bans diesel trucks older than BS-VI from entering Delhi, halts most construction and demolition, and lets schools move primary classes online.

steps.text: Pollution builds when cold air near the ground stops rising and mixing.
Delhi sits in a basin, so smoke and dust collect instead of blowing away.
Farm fires add a burst of smoke in late October and November.
GRAP cuts the local sources it controls: vehicles, dust and diesel generators.

items.meaning: seven times the level India calls 'satisfactory' (under 50 is 'good')
rough share of Delhi's winter PM2.5 that comes from vehicles

items.view: Says early action on local sources prevents the worst 'severe plus' days.
Say the truck ban hurts small operators who cannot afford new vehicles, while farm fires go unpunished.

for_you.text: If you live in Delhi-NCR, expect costlier vegetables as truck entry is restricted, slower construction, and possible online classes for young children. An N95 mask, not a cloth one, filters the fine particles that matter.

next.text: CAQM reviews the stage daily. If AQI crosses 450 it moves to Stage IV, which adds odd-even style limits.
unknowns: How long the still weather lasts

terms.meaning: Air Quality Index: one number summarising several pollutants, higher is worse
Delhi's four-stage emergency plan that tightens rules as air worsens

check.q: Why does Delhi's air get worse in winter?
options: Cold, still air traps pollution near the ground
check.why: Cold air near the ground stops rising, so smoke and dust collect over the city.

sources.excerpt: The 24-hour average AQI for Delhi stood at 362.
CAQM invokes Stage-III of extant GRAP in the entire Delhi-NCR with immediate effect.
Satellite data recorded 1,840 farm fires in Punjab this week.
Vehicles contribute roughly a third of PM2.5 in winter.

scenes.say: Delhi just banned older diesel trucks. Will that actually clear the air?
The air quality index crossed three hundred and fifty. That is seven times the level called satisfactory.
In winter, cold still air acts like a lid. Smoke from farm fires, traffic and dust gets trapped over the city.
The emergency plan cuts what Delhi controls: trucks, building dust, generators. It can't stop the weather.
If the index crosses four fifty, stricter limits follow. Wear an N ninety five, not a cloth mask.

lesson.concept: How a central bank rate reaches your EMI
lesson.big_idea: When the central bank changes its rate, banks change what they charge, and a floating-rate loan's EMI follows a few months later.

steps.title: The policy rate
steps.text: The Fed or the RBI sets the rate at which banks borrow overnight. It is the base price of money.

steps.title: Banks pass it on
steps.text: Banks link loan rates to that base. A floating-rate home loan moves when the benchmark moves.

steps.title: Your EMI is recalculated
steps.text: At the next reset, the bank recalculates your monthly instalment, or keeps it and changes the loan length.

example.setup: Say you have a ₹50 lakh home loan over 20 years and the rate falls from 9% to 8.75%.
example.result: A quarter-point cut saves about ₹800 a month on a ₹50 lakh loan.

apply.text: The Fed held its rate, so there is no push from Washington for the RBI to cut soon, and floating-rate EMIs stay where they are for now.

practice.q: On a ₹25 lakh loan, roughly how much would the same cut save each month?
practice.answer: Half the loan, so about half the saving: around ₹400 a month, or ₹4,800 a year.
